title: Current weight is mandatory on every paediatric surgical episode
logic: If a surgical episode is opened for a patient under 12 years and no weight measured within the current presentation is recorded, drug dosing, fluid prescription, and anaesthesia cannot be safely calculated.
action: Make current measured weight a required field before theatre booking or any weight-based prescription; flag estimated weights explicitly as estimates.

title: Electrolyte correction gates pyloromyotomy booking
logic: If pyloromyotomy is being booked and the most recent electrolytes do not document corrected hypochloraemic alkalosis (chloride and bicarbonate within the unit's accepted pre-anaesthetic range), the infant is not theatre-ready — anaesthetising the uncorrected infant risks postoperative apnoea.
action: Block theatre listing until a post-resuscitation electrolyte result within range is attached; display the correction status on the booking; there is no emergency override — the surgical condition itself is never the emergency.

title: Bilious vomiting in a neonate is malrotation until excluded
logic: If green (bilious) vomiting is recorded in a neonate or young infant, midgut malrotation with volvulus is the presumed diagnosis; the midgut can infarct within hours.
action: Raise an emergency alert; nasogastric decompression, intravenous resuscitation, and immediate surgical referral; upper GI contrast only if the child is stable and it will not delay theatre or transfer; block any pathway that assigns this presentation to routine observation.

title: Irreducible inguinal hernia in an infant
logic: If a paediatric inguinal hernia is recorded as irreducible, tender, or associated with vomiting or a red overlying scrotum/groin, incarceration threatening bowel and testis is presumed.
action: Emergency surgical referral; allow one senior-supervised attempt at taxis with analgesia in the non-toxic child; failed reduction or toxicity routes straight to theatre; successful reduction still books repair on the same admission.

title: Hirschsprung-associated enterocolitis pattern
logic: If a child with confirmed or suspected Hirschsprung disease develops abdominal distension with fever, lethargy, or foul explosive diarrhoea, Hirschsprung-associated enterocolitis is presumed — it is the leading killer in this disease.
action: Alert for emergency management: resuscitation, broad-spectrum antibiotics including anaerobic cover, rectal washouts (not enemas under pressure), and urgent surgical review for possible emergency stoma; escalate scheduling of any pending definitive surgery discussion.

title: Anorectal malformation level drives the operative pathway
logic: If an anorectal malformation is recorded, classify by level within 24–48 hours of birth: visible perineal fistula with meconium classifies LOW (candidate for primary anoplasty under experienced assessment); no visible fistula, meconium in urine, or a flat perineum classifies HIGH (divided sigmoid colostomy now, staged PSARP later at specialist centre).
action: Present the level-classification checklist on the neonatal record; route HIGH classifications to emergency colostomy booking and specialist referral; attach the associated-anomaly (VACTERL) screening bundle to every classification.

title: Weight-based single-dose prophylaxis for paediatric surgery
logic: If a paediatric surgical procedure is booked, prophylaxis is a single weight-calculated intravenous dose of cefazolin within 60 minutes before incision, adding metronidazole for any bowel-opening or contaminated procedure; clean minor day-cases may omit prophylaxis per unit policy; established peritonitis (typhoid perforation, gangrenous intussusception) uses a treatment course instead.
action: Prompt weight-calculated prophylaxis at induction using the recorded current weight; alert if the ordered dose does not match the weight-based calculation; suppress the prompt when a treatment course is charted.

title: Paediatric postoperative physiology and fluid surveillance
logic: If a child is postoperative from abdominal surgery, age-appropriate paediatric early-warning observations are due at least hourly for 4 hours then per protocol, with strict fluid balance (maintenance plus measured losses, glucose-containing fluids for neonates) and nasogastric/stoma output replacement; neonates additionally need temperature and glucose checks because cold and hypoglycaemia kill quietly.
action: Generate the age-banded observation and fluid-balance task schedule at ward return; alert on paediatric early-warning breaches, on any neonate temperature or glucose excursion, and on stoma/nasogastric outputs not reflected in the fluid prescription.

title: Ex-premature infants need postoperative apnoea monitoring
logic: If an infant below the unit's corrected-gestational-age threshold (commonly under about 60 weeks post-conceptional age) undergoes anaesthesia, day-case discharge is unsafe — postoperative apnoea risk mandates overnight saturation and apnoea monitoring.
action: At booking, compute corrected age from recorded gestation and birth date; block day-case pathway selection for infants under threshold and reserve a monitored bed instead.

title: Orchidopexy outcome review at 6–12 months
logic: If orchidopexy has been performed, a follow-up at 6–12 months documenting testicular position and size (atrophy check) is part of the operation's outcome, alongside early wound review; adolescents are additionally taught self-examination.
action: Auto-book the early wound review and the 6–12 month position-and-size review at operation coding; flag operations with no outcome review recorded by 15 months; attach the adolescent self-examination education item to the record for later delivery.
